subject: MSA redline: Reckless conduct & fraud carve-outs — proposal and next steps
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com>
To: Elena Gomez <egomez@fintechx.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 21 Jul 2026 09:02:00 -0700
Subject: MSA redline: Reckless conduct & fraud carve-outs — proposal and next steps

Hi Elena,

Thanks again for taking time this morning. Per our conversation, attached is the redlined MSA with the sections we discussed around limitation of liability and carve-outs (Sections 9 and 10 in this draft). High level summary of the suggested approach:

- Keep a single overall cap tied to paid fees over the prior 12 months as a default, but introduce explicit carve-outs for willful misconduct and proven fraud (uncapped for direct damages tied to fraudulent acts).
- Narrow the "gross negligence" term and, alternatively, provide an explicit definition for "reckless conduct" so both sides understand the threshold. Our proposed compromise is to require a showing of (i) willful intent, or (ii) recklessness that is manifested by repeated disregard for known material controls and results in material harm.
- For reckless conduct that does not meet the willful/fraud standard, propose a separate sub-cap: the greater of $500,000 or 3x paid fees in the prior 12 months, but only where the conduct is tied to a material breach.
- Maintain a firm exclusion for consequential and punitive damages except where statutory or the occurence stems from willful misconduct/fraud.
- Add a procedural requirement: materiality showing (written notice + 30-day cure) before pursuing damages that exceed the baseline cap. This preserves ops continuity.

Attached files: redlined-MSA-20260721.docx (tracked changes).

Next steps: Would you and Marta be able to review the attached language and tell us whether the "$500k or 3x fees" sub-cap for recklessness is a non-starter? If so, provide your preferred threshold and brief rationale. If you prefer, we can hop on a 30-minute call tomorrow with Marissa and Lauren (legal) to walk through language line-by-line.

Thanks,

--
Karthik Iyer
Enterprise Account Executive

From: Elena Gomez <egomez@fintechx.com>

Date: Tue, 21 Jul 2026 12:30:00 -04:00
Subject: Re: MSA redline: Reckless conduct & fraud carve-outs — proposal and next steps

Karthik,

Appreciate the summary and the redline. A few quick reactions from our side:

- Our legal team is comfortable with an uncapped carve-out for proven intentional fraud, but we need much tighter language around "reckless" — the word is very fact-intensive and could be abused.
- We cannot accept a cap that is calculated on the prior 12 months' fees for the sole remedy in all reckless situations. For example, if there's an incident affecting core payment rails, the harm could be multiples beyond fees.
- Would your team consider a two-tier approach: (A) uncapped for willful misconduct/fraud; (B) for reckless conduct, a sub-cap equal to the greater of $1M or 5x the fees in the prior 12 months, but only if the conduct is proven by clear and convincing evidence?

We will review the specific language and follow up with a marked counter. In parallel, Marta is pulling any vendor risk memos we have that reference similar carve-outs.

Elena
Head of Procurement
FinTechX
egomez@fintechx.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwoodinference.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, 22 Jul 2026 08:15:00 -07:00
Subject: Internal: draft language for reckless/willful/fraud carve-outs (see attached)

Karthik — quick internal note before we respond to FinTechX. I reviewed their ask and sketched alternative text to reduce ambiguity. Key points and recommended language:

1) Definitions: Replace undefined terms. Add: "Willful Misconduct" means a deliberate act or omission with knowledge that such act or omission is unlawful or will likely cause material harm. "Reckless Conduct" means conduct demonstrating a conscious disregard of a substantial and unjustifiable risk that such conduct will cause material harm, measured by: (i) prior written warnings; (ii) repeated disregard for documented operational controls; and (iii) evidence of gross departure from industry-standard practices.

2) Caps and carve-outs:
- Baseline Cap: total liability limited to the greater of (A) $750,000 or (B) twelve (12) months of fees paid under the Order Form immediately preceding the claim.
- Recklessness Sub-Cap: for claims that meet the definition of Reckless Conduct but not Willful Misconduct/Fraud, sub-cap of the greater of $750,000 or 3x fees in prior 12 months — but only where the claimant demonstrates material breach after cure period.
- Fraud/Willful Misconduct: uncapped for direct damages caused by proven Fraud or Willful Misconduct (subject to indemnity procedures).

3) Burden and standard: For Reckless Conduct claims, require clear and convincing evidence and a documented notice + 30 day cure window; if unresolved, the parties may engage an independent forensic auditor (mutually agreeable) whose report will bind the parties for purposes of the cap. Cost of the auditor borne by prevailing party unless auditor finds misconduct by both.

4) Operational guardrails: add a short SLA carve acknowledging that mitigation steps taken in good faith will reduce liability exposure (e.g., timely incident response, offering credits, root cause analysis).

Attached: legal-annot-msa.docx with line edits and a short memo. If FinTechX pushes to $1M/5x, I think we can counter with $750k/3x + auditor and higher evidentiary standard. That combination reduces risk while giving them recourse for severe incidents.

LMK if you want me on the call to walk through line edits.

-Marissa
Director, Legal Ops
Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com>

Date: Wed, 22 Jul 2026 14:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: MSA redline: Reckless conduct & fraud carve-outs — proposal and next steps

Elena,

Thanks for the quick note and for surfacing Marta. We appreciate the sensitivity around defining "reckless." Based on Marissa's input, here's a pragmatic compromise we think aligns incentives and addresses FinTechX's risk concerns without exposing Redwood to open-ended liabilities:

- Baseline cap: greater of $750k or 12 months' fees (keeps commercial predictability).
- Reckless conduct: sub-cap equal to greater of $750k or 3x fees in prior 12 months. Recklessness is defined as in the attached legal memo and must be shown by clear and convincing evidence; claimants must provide written notice and a 30-day cure period before escalating to damages beyond the baseline cap.
- Willful misconduct/fraud: uncapped for direct damages where fraud or willful intent is proven by a preponderance of evidence (we can accept a lower standard here to address your concerns).
- Consequential/punitive damages remain excluded except where law requires otherwise or where damages arise directly from proven willful misconduct/fraud.
- Independent forensic auditor option: either party can request an auditor if the facts are in dispute; auditor's findings bind remedies for purposes of cap calculation.

We believe this addresses the scenarios you called out (e.g., systemic payment exposure) while keeping a workable commercial cap for the majority of operational incidents. If that sounds acceptable in principle, Marissa can convert the language to redline-ready text for your counsel. We can also route the Order Form for signature via DocuSign once redlines are agreed. DocuSign preview: https://app.docusign.com/someDocId/abcdef

Would you prefer Marissa to send the next tracked-change version or shall I loop in our procurement ops person to start preparing the SOW/Order Form? Happy to do either.

Best,

--
Karthik
Redwood Inference

Karthik and team,

Thanks — that compromise is directionally acceptable. A few small follow-ups before we sign:

1) We'd prefer the proof standard for Fraud/Willful Misconduct to be "clear and convincing" rather than preponderance. If you can accept that, it eases our board-level sign-off.
2) For the Reckless sub-cap, FinTechX will accept $750k or 3x fees in the prior 12 months provided: (a) the independent forensic auditor mechanism is final and binding for the cap calculation, and (b) Redwood agrees to a one-time accelerated remediation commitment (2x the standard incident response staffing for 30 days) if the auditor finds reckless conduct.
3) Attached is a one-page counter-redline with these two bullets called out (counter-redline.pdf).

If Marissa can slip that into the draft and share a final tracked version, procurement and I will run it through signatures. Please route the Order Form via DocuSign when ready.

Elena
Head of Procurement
FinTechX
